assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology led to incretin therapies that have transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with large cardiovascular and renal outcome benefits. The path from hormone discovery to receptor-agonist drugs is clear, original and of very broad clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1), Drucker (actions, intestinotrophic and cardiometabolic biology) and Mojsov (identification of the active peptide GLP-1(7-36) and its insulinotropic role) form a defensible trio. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen led the industrial development of liraglutide and semaglutide, which makes a fourth-name case; credit between academic discovery and drug development is contested.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by multiple independent trials and by years of use in millions of patients, with consistent mechanistic understanding. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue given the scale of impact.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over the early GLP-1 peptide work, notably Mojsov versus others, are not fully settled in my knowledge.
Whether the committee wishes to honor drug development (Knudsen) alongside the basic discovery; the three-name cap forces exclusion.
I have not verified details of the priority record independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of living drugs. The concept is original and the clinical impact is clear, with ongoing extension to autoimmune disease.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early CAR design with costimulation), June (clinical translation, CD19 CAR-T in CLL and ALL) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T-cell therapy) cover concept, translation and the cell-therapy foundation. Eshhar, Kuwana and others are not on the supplied credit list, so I cannot propose them.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent long-term follow-up support durability. Toxicity, manufacturing limits and relapse are active issues but do not undermine the core achievement.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among early chimeric-receptor work, costimulatory design and clinical translation is contested.
Efficacy in solid tumors remains limited, so the scope of the discovery is still evolving.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Microbial opsins used to control genetically defined cells with light gave neuroscience a causal, millisecond-precision tool, and have reshaped circuit studies across organisms. This is a transformative method with wide use, though it is a tool rather than a disease mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin identification and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and the neuronal implementation and systems-level use (Deisseroth, Boyden) are both decisive. Six credited names exceed the three-laureate limit, and Miesenböck's earlier genetically targeted photostimulation adds further complexity. I select the channelrhodopsin discovery and the leading neuronal application, with real uncertainty.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed and in routine use for over a decade, with early clinical translation (vision restoration). Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among six credited names is unresolved and a three-person prize would omit key contributors.
Medical impact is still emerging relative to impact on research.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle vaccines against HPV prevent persistent infection and cervical and other cancers, with population-level evidence of sharply reduced precancer and cancer incidence. This is a clear, original and highly consequential preventive-medicine achievement.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity) and Frazer (early VLP work and translation) are the credited names. Others who contributed to the VLP work are not on the supplied list, so the allocation relies on the supplied credit; some uncertainty about the fairness of the trio remains.
assessment.maturity: Strong, independent confirmation from national vaccination programs showing reductions in infection, CIN2+ and now invasive cancer. Timing is mature, and the cancer-outcome data have strengthened.
uncertainties: Priority and credit among several groups working on papillomavirus VLPs in the early 1990s is contested.
Recognition of the 2008 prize for HPV as a cause of cervical cancer may influence the committee's view of this topic.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new form of organelle-to-nucleus signaling, using IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing and related branches, and links ER stress to metabolic disease, neurodegeneration and cancer. The discovery is original, conceptually clean and widely taught.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori identified the signal transduction pathway through IRE1 and HAC1 and the unconventional mRNA splicing mechanism, so two names capture the decisive work. Contributions from other groups (such as Ron on PERK/eIF2 and Wang) are not credited on the list, so cannot be added.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed over three decades in yeast and mammals. Therapeutic translation is incomplete, but the basic discovery is mature and stable.
uncertainties: Clinical impact is indirect so far, which may weigh against it in a medicine context.
Allocation versus other UPR branches is outside the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition provided the first strong proof that a molecularly targeted drug can turn a fatal cancer into a manageable chronic disease. The principle of targeting a driver kinase has been validated repeatedly.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical development and the case for ABL inhibition), Lydon (medicinal chemistry and kinase inhibitor program) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) form a plausible trio. Rowley, Witte, Konopka and others who identified BCR-ABL are not credited here, and the discovery has previously been honored via Lasker awards in a shared form.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with long-term survival data from many thousands of patients and independent replication. Timing is late but the case is solid.
uncertainties: Chemistry versus clinical development credit, particularly the role of Jürg Zimmermann and others, is not captured in the supplied names.
Part of the underlying story (BCR-ABL fusion) may be seen as already recognized by earlier work, which may reduce the novelty of this specific candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TNF as a driver of inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis and proof that its blockade is effective established cytokine-targeted therapy in autoimmune disease, and anti-TNF agents became among the best-selling drugs. The work is original and has transformed care.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini carried out the central translational work, from showing TNF's role in synovial cytokine networks to the clinical trials of infliximab. The supplied credit is a clean two-person pairing, though contributions of Kollias, Vilcek, Cerami and others raise allocation questions that the list does not resolve.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation over two decades with multiple agents and indications. Mature and stable.
uncertainties: Credit for the TNF discovery and antibody development (e.g., Vilcek's monoclonal antibody) is outside the supplied list and could be disputed.
Prior Lasker recognition does not remove the question of how the prize would be framed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 revealed that cancer can arise from blocked cell death rather than only increased proliferation, defined the BCL-2 family as the control point of mitochondrial apoptosis, and led to venetoclax. The discovery is conceptually important and has direct clinical consequences.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams cloned and characterized the BCL-2 translocation context and family biology, and Vaux demonstrated that BCL-2 promotes survival and cooperates with MYC. Strasser is also credited and played a major role; the three-name limit forces a choice. Tsujimoto's cloning of BCL-2 and Korsmeyer's contributions are not on the list.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed, with an approved targeted therapy and extensive independent follow-up. Apoptosis has been recognized before (2002) which does not preclude this topic, but may affect framing.
uncertainties: Credit among Cory, Adams, Vaux and Strasser is hard to separate, and early independent cloning by other groups is not credited in the list.
Some of the contribution lies in the broader apoptosis field already awarded in 2002.
